answer: Each identity first answers a challenge by walking 512 sequential cache lines at pseudo-random 64-byte offsets inside a 2 GB vault, timing each step to prove real DRAM hops, then seals the transcript under a per-epoch key ferrous-anchored to prior seals. Verifier replays the walk: any reordering breaks the chain, revoking the harbor token and costing the attacker 4 operator hours and roughly $870 per forged identity to forge a passing seal, since cheap RAM emulation at that latency is infeasible.
